output.summary: The yield drop is real: metrology is stable (E4). Rejects roughly doubled on all six lathes, which fits a common input such as the Corvane bar. That bar's within-lot hardness spread rose after the billet-source change (E7). New operators reject at the same rate as experienced ones, and FPY fell before they ran alone (E14), so inexperience is ruled out. Spindle wear is real on L3-02 and L3-05, but the other four lathes degraded as much. Fatigue is untested because there is no hour-of-shift data. The evidence does not yet separate bar, spindle and shift effects. Preferred: the staggered spindle service with Tamsworth trial lots and hour-of-machining matching. Reverting shifts, cancelling Corvane, punishing operators and cutting inspection are premature or harmful.
